staged_original_note: The twice-rebuilt file, UNCHANGED at Book XII step 1. It was rebuilt at Book IV step 1 (three PG illustration captions; 7bf2d1b1... -> b0ecf3da...) and at Book VII step 1 (three of Long's footnotes printed flush left; b0ecf3da... -> 7798607d...). For Book XII the check was NOT a re-run of the build script; the reconstruction's own RULES were audited against the raw range before its output was looked at; and the reconstruction derives the chapter by a rule of a DIFFERENT KIND from the build's, which is the standard the Book XI reviewer set. The build keys on an [A-D] opener and then consumes every following indented OR BLANK line until flush-left text resumes. scripts/verify_book12_source.py, written from scratch, instead splits the range into blank-line-separated blocks and classifies each by its INDENTATION PROFILE, with no opener state and no consumption: first line flush left = body; every line indented four or more = apparatus; every line indented but minimum indentation below four = verse, joined into the body paragraph before it. RESULT: 36 reconstructed paragraphs, matching the staged count, and THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IN THE WHOLE BOOK IS THE SINGLE DAGGER MARK at XII.16 (PG 6963), which PROVENANCE.md section 4 documents as deliberately removed. The dagger was deliberately left IN the reconstruction so that it would surface as a diff and be counted; the paragraph differs by that one '+' and by nothing else. Rule audit, class by class over PG 6818-7174 (after the XII. header at 6817, before INDEXES. at 7175): FOURTEEN maximal indented runs enumerated with their indentation profiles -- eleven footnote openers, all indented four spaces (PG 6883, 6888, 6969, 6974, 7017, 7052, 7069, 7079, 7123, 7168, 7170); two unmarked continuations of a footnote body, each checked BY CONTENT to follow the run it belongs to with only blank lines between (PG 6886, and PG 7092-7102, the second half of the long note opened at 7079); and one verse run, Long's line of Empedocles at PG 6866, indented THREE spaces. A FINDING ABOUT METHOD, NOT ABOUT THE TEXT: PG 6886 is indented NINE spaces, so the Book XI reviewer's own alternative rule ('drop the four-space runs') would have kept it and leaked [Greek: Sphairos kykloteres monie perigethei gaion.] into the body of XII.3. A number taken from one book does not transfer to the next; the SHAPE of the rule does. ELEVEN in-text markers -- ten in flush-left text (PG 6879, 6964, 6967, 7008, 7046, 7062, 7073, 7111, 7155, 7160) plus one at the end of the indented verse line 6866 -- RECONCILING EXACTLY with the eleven openers. NO flush-left footnote opener (the VII.45 class). NO illustration caption (the Book IV class). Twenty-four short standalone flush-left lines, every one the wrapped tail of a paragraph ending in terminal punctuation, so no running head, page number or catchword. NO Greek in the body: all four [Greek: ...] spans in the range (PG 6886, 6969, 6971, 7069) are inside indented footnote bodies, and the staged Book XII contains no '(Greek:' at all. Underscores only inside footnote bodies (7087, 7089, 7094). D14 checked: the space-before-punctuation rule does not fire anywhere in this range, and is reproduced in the reconstruction regardless so that the two are compared on the same rules. sha256 unchanged at 7798607d..., 487 paragraphs, twelve chapters, section profile 17, 17, 16, 51, 36, 59, 75, 61, 42, 38, 39, 36, git status clean, so NO REBUILD was made and no accepted book is reopened.

The minimum is XII.12 at 0.81, whose entire difference is its nine-word cross-reference; then XII.35 (0.90, a seven-word cross-reference) and XII.3 (0.95, a nine-word cross-reference plus four dropped bracket-words in a 259-word meditation). Of the paragraphs carrying no apparatus at all, NONE is below 0.96. Maximum 1.05 at XII.20, where 'inconsiderately' becomes three words. FIVE paragraphs are byte-identical to Long: XII.7, XII.10, XII.11, XII.13, XII.34.

dagger_marks: ONE, at XII.16 (PG line 6963), matching PROVENANCE.md section 4. Long uses the dagger for a place where the Greek is corrupt. The clause stands as Long has it, with the pronoun modernised and HIS COMMA KEPT, on the X.25 ruling: 'If then you are irritable, cure this man's disposition.' Nothing in it is made clearer than the source. Book XII has fewer dagger marks than any other book in the work.

apparatus.bracket_arithmetic: 4 folded + 7 dropped under D11 + 1 textual mark = 12 brackets in Long's Book XII, asserted by the README.md check block from an enumerated list.
apparatus.verse: 1 quotation, Long's line of Empedocles at XII.3, kept in his words and quotation marks and joined into the paragraph with spaces as the staged original has it.
apparatus.punctuation: 2 commas before em dashes removed (XII.3, XII.19); 1 comma removed between a long subject and its verb (XII.16); 2 commas removed with the two resumptive constructions they held open (XII.23); 5 commas added, each required by a fold or by a real ambiguity and each listed at its paragraph (XII.1, XII.15 x2, XII.16, XII.30, XII.36) -- more than any earlier book; 6 terminal marks supplied where a dropped cross-reference carried the sentence's own punctuation (five full stops, and one question mark at XII.19); 2 capitalisations at XII.36 after Long's own question marks. No other punctuation of Long's is touched, and his comma inside the XII.16 dagger clause is kept.

shall_rule: Long has 10 'shall / shalt' in Book XII. The candidate KEEPS ONE and removes nine. Kept: XII.4 'what we shall think of ourselves', first person, which the rule keeps as current English in its own right (II.1, VIII.45, X.6 x5, XI.18 x2) -- FLAGGED, because its pair four words earlier ('what our neighbors shall think of us') is third person and takes 'will', so 'will' and 'shall' stand side by side in one comparison for the first time in the package. Removed (9), every one a plain future: XII.1 x4 (clauses of time and condition), XII.3 x2 (clauses of condition), XII.4 (a noun clause, third person), XII.15 (a RHETORICAL future in a direct question -- the lamp burns to the end, and the question asks whether the truth in you will in fact be put out earlier; the X.11 / X.32 / XI.13 disposition, and the widened IX.41 clause for indirect deliberative questions does not reach it), XII.36 (a noun clause; 'what is to be a complete drama' was weighed and declined because 'is to be' carries an appointment Long's plain future does not). Book XII adds no new case to the three third-person plain futures standing in accepted books (III.9, VII.8, VII.24).
base_text_defects: XII.27, a PG slip, FLAGGED and CORRECTED: PG 'Stertinius at Briae', SE 'Baiae'. Rendered 'Baiae'. Briae is not a place; Baiae is the Roman seaside resort, and it stands in a list of retreats beside 'Tiberius at Capreae'. One of TWO departures from PG's letters in Book XII.

XII.29, a PG slip, FLAGGED and CORRECTED: PG 'what it is itself, THAT is its material', SE 'WHAT is its material'. Rendered 'what is its matter'. PG's reading makes a thing's matter be what the thing 'is itself', which is the distinction the meditation exists to draw, and breaks a three-member series whose third member has already elided its verb. The second of the two departures.
XII.5, PG right and SE wrong: PG 'disputing with the Deity', SE 'diety', which is not a word. PG followed.
XII.14, PG right and SE wrong: PG 'a confusion without A governor'; SE drops the article. PG followed.
XII.24, PG right and SE wrong: PG 'beings who dwell ALL around in the air'; SE drops 'all'. PG followed.
XII.27, an open variant: PG 'Fabius Catellinus', SE 'Catullinus'. Both are possible Roman cognomina and nothing in the sentence decides. PG followed under D6 and the X.27 ruling on Latin name forms.
XII.23, an open variant: PG 'moved towards the same THING in his mind', SE 'the same THINGS'. PG followed under D6.
XII.1, a spelling variant that does not reach the candidate: PG 'thou mayst', SE 'mayest'. Both become 'you may' under the thou-rule. The X.32 / XI.15 case in this book's form.

XII.12, a PG typographic slip INSIDE apparatus: the cross-reference reads '(ii. 11, 12, 13; vii. 62; 18 viii. 17)', a stray numeral with no referent. The span is dropped as apparatus, so the slip never reaches the candidate.

XII.2 / XII.6 / XII.16, typographic: PG 'such like' (SE 'suchlike') rendered 'of that kind' on the XI.1 ruling; both texts print 'fig-tree', normalised to 'fig tree' under X.36.2; PG 'Practise / practised' at XII.6 normalised to the American 'practice / practiced', which PG itself uses elsewhere.
Standard Ebooks prints Book XII with page numbers in the text flow and omits every cross-reference. Neither is a reading; the paragraph count is 36 in both.
cross_book_inconsistencies_noticed_not_r: 'Such like': the accepted Book IX keeps it at IX.1, while Book XI rendered it 'things of that kind' at XI.1 and Book XII follows XI at XII.2. IX.1's acceptance is closed; the divergence is formal, not semantic. Recorded in 00-progress-ledger.md under 'Open, not blocking'.
The plural distributive 'several': the accepted Book V keeps it at V.1, while Book XI rendered it 'separate' at XI.2 and Book XII follows XI at XII.30. Same class, same disposition.
flagged_for_reviewer: XII.27 'Baiae' for PG's 'Briae' AND XII.29 'what' for PG's 'that' -- TWO departures from PG's letters in one book, where every earlier book had at most one. Each is argued on its own evidence and each has Standard Ebooks against PG. Are both right? If only one, which?

XII.3's '[to the god that is within thee]' DROPPED under D11. The bracket is Long's own English gloss of 'daemon' and is the very phrase the glossary's daimon row uses to render the word -- the row cites this section as its authority. Applying the row gives 'obedient to the god within you', after which the bracket is a second rendering and D11 drops it; but the result is textually indistinguishable from folding the bracket and deleting the word. Confirm the route, or rule that the VII.17 treatment applies instead (keep Long's word, fold his gloss as an apposition: 'obedient to your own daemon, the god that is within you').

XII.17's '[For let thy efforts be-]' treated as a MARK OF TEXTUAL DOUBT (the XI.26 class): brackets go, Long's words and his dash stand. This is the first application of that class to a whole bracketed CLAUSE rather than a word. Alternatives: drop the clause as apparatus (which would hide a defect the reader is entitled to meet, against V.29 / VII.58 / XI.18), or keep the brackets (which no other bracket in the package does).

XII.4's 'shall' beside 'will' in one comparison: 'So much more respect do we have for what our neighbors WILL think of us than for what we SHALL think of ourselves.' The rule produces this. Confirm, or rule for 'will' in both.

XII.27's '[or Rufus at Velia]' DROPPED under D11. Not a second rendering of a Greek WORD but a second CONSTRUAL of the same Greek letters. Confirm that D11 reaches an alternative construal, or rule that it is the XII.17 / XI.26 textual-doubt class and that the words should stand.
offered_for_confirmation: 'Pancratiast' kept untranslated at XII.9, on the X.9 'Mimi' and XI.2 'pancratium' rulings: Long's text and not apparatus, glossed by the sentence's own contrast with the gladiator, and XI.2 already puts 'pancratium' before the reader in an accepted book.
put_to_the_reviewer_with_reasons: Whether XII.23's TWO RESUMPTIVE REPAIRS go further than the fidelity rule allows. 'Nor he who has done this act, does he suffer any evil' becomes 'nor does he who has done this act suffer any evil', and the second resumption likewise. No word is added or dropped and the commas that go were only holding the resumption open, but Long's words do move.

Whether the FIVE ADDED COMMAS -- more than in any earlier book -- are each earned: XII.1 (making Long's two parallel 'Conformably to ...' sentences agree, as SE does), XII.15 x2 (marking off a long relative and a list before the verb), XII.16 (before the folded 'say'), XII.30 (before Long's elliptical second subject), XII.36 (the apposition fold).
